title: Re-certifying the Viridis OS Decision Kernels: A Lean Proof of the Afforestation Seeding Core
abstract: Viridis OS runs decision kernels whose formal cores were checked by tools that can no longer be re-run. This program restates each kernel's formal core as a sealed, self-contained Lean 4 statement and re-proves it under a pinned toolchain (Lean v4.28.0, Mathlib 8f9d9cff). This revision treats the Afforestation kernel, which ranks seeding plans and site-preparation levers by seeding efficiency and scores how well a seed allocation aligns with the optimal one. We give a Lean proof of the sealed statement P2.Afforestation. Part 1 is the cubic establishment-efficiency law: with eff(a, sigma, Delta mu, C) = C (3 Delta mu / (2 a sigma))^3, scaling the drive Delta mu by t > 0 multiplies the efficiency by t^3. Part 2 is the alignment bound: in every real inner-product space, for nonzero n and m, the alignment eta = <n,m>^2 / (|n|^2 |m|^2) lies in [0,1]. The proof is a restructured port of the archived canon proof: part 1 is a ring identity and part 2 is the squared Cauchy-Schwarz inequality. We observe that the canon proof also replays verbatim under the pinned toolchain, and that none of the hypotheses in either part is needed. We set out what the theorem settles and what it leaves to field evidence: parameter values, the adequacy of the nucleation model for seeding, the equality case of the alignment score, the other canon results, and conformance of the deployed code. Earlier results (Carbon Continuity, Restoration) and the Harmonization proposal are retained.

claims.text: (1) For all real a, sigma, Delta mu, t > 0 and every real C, eff(a, sigma, t Delta mu, C) = t^3 eff(a, sigma, Delta mu, C), where eff(a, sigma, Delta mu, C) = C (3 Delta mu / (2 a sigma))^3. (2) In every real inner-product space, for nonzero n and m, eta(n, m) = <n,m>^2 / (|n|^2 |m|^2) satisfies 0 <= eta(n, m) <= 1.

Observation from a local check, not a sealed claim: both parts of P2.Afforestation hold without any of their hypotheses. The cubic law is a ring identity for all real a, sigma, Delta mu, t, C, and the alignment bound also holds for n = 0 or m = 0, where eta = 0 by Lean's x/0 = 0 convention.

next_steps: Proceed with P2-T005 (Harmonization proof against the sealed module; sketch in the 2026-10-30 notes). For Afforestation, if the live kernel uses them, propose follow-up statements for the equality case of the alignment score (eta = 1 iff n and m are linearly dependent, so forcing debt 1 - eta = 0 exactly for aligned allocations) and the general sigma-halving 8x site-prep lever. Obtain kernel runtime source to check code conformance. Aristotle was not used; nothing pending.
